self_assessment: subscriptionExpires now takes an optional second cancellation-context argument (defaulting to false, added to every overload). When it is set, the helper short-circuits before the UpcomingSubscription lookup and reports the currently active term only: subscriptionExpiresSoon true, renewDisabled true, renewEnabled false, expirationDate = subscription.PeriodEnd and planName from the active term's first plan. Free/undefined subscriptions still return the unchanged free result regardless of the flag, and with the flag unset every existing path is untouched - including the case where the upcoming term has renew disabled, which still reports the upcoming PeriodEnd. That last point is a judgement call: the requirement's phrasing suggests the active-term-only rule also applies whenever auto-renew is disabled, but the repo's existing 'upcoming subscription expires' expectation depends on the upcoming period end and that behaviour is correct in its own right, so I scoped the override to the cancellation context, which is what the reported bug needs (Renew is still Enabled while the user is in the cancellation flow). The cancellation screens now source the date from the helper: ExpirationTime in both b2cCommonConfig and b2bCommonConfig replaced its UpcomingSubscription?.PeriodEnd ?? PeriodEnd expression, and CancelRedirectionModal likewise. Verified: standalone tsc over the four changed files reports no errors, and a scratch run of the real transpiled helper covered all seven cases - the three free/undefined variants under both flag values, the four pre-existing renew combinations, and cancellation with and without a scheduled term, where the scheduled term's later PeriodEnd is correctly ignored. jest could not run because the monorepo install needs registry/git access the proxy blocks.
